tldr: Google Cloud showed startups running real-time world models on TPUs in mid-October. At PyTorch Conference on Oct 25, Google and Meta open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for TPUs, and a Google agent-network repo surfaced three days later.
whats_new: InfoQ's Nov 2 deep dive says TorchTPU runs PyTorch workloads on TPU hardware with minimal code modification, a second report on the Oct 25 Google-Meta open-source release.
why_it_matters: A native PyTorch path to TPUs lowers the porting cost of treating TPUs as a second accelerator target next to GPUs.

status.detail: TorchTPU is open-sourced; independent reports of production use and benchmarks are still missing.

beats.headline: TPUs as a target for real-time generative workloads
Google and Meta open-source TorchTPU for native PyTorch on TPUs
Google publishes Agentmesh, an open-source zero-trust agent network
Follow-up coverage details how TorchTPU works

open_questions: Do independent benchmarks show TorchTPU matching GPU PyTorch performance on LLM workloads?
Does Meta move larger LLM workloads onto TPUs with TorchTPU, as it said it plans to?
take_for_builders: If you run PyTorch on GPUs, test a representative model on TorchTPU to measure porting effort before relying on it; wait for independent benchmarks before committing capacity.
